original_text: Washington, D.C. — The Trump administration ordered the removal of 60 historic cherry trees from East Potomac Park early Tuesday morning to make way for a renovation of the East Potomac Golf Links. The work began at 5:30 a.m., before a federal judge could hold a scheduled hearing on a temporary restraining order. Chainsaws and wood chippers were used to clear a row of trees along the seventh fairway. All 60 trees were Japanese cherry trees, including 45 descended from the 1912 gift from Tokyo and 15 planted in the 1980s. A park volunteer said the trees were gone within three hours. Internal emails show the removal was requested by the golf course renovation team and approved by a senior Interior Department official. The project is part of a $12 million plan to redesign the course. No court order was issued before the cutting began.
